value.quote: we look for subgame-perfect Nash equilibria
value.note: Main results characterise subgame-perfect equilibrium outcomes of procedures and evaluate them against utilitarian efficiency; agenda-setters' strategic proposal-making is analysed only through equilibrium, not as a separate incentive/manipulation result, so SB is not coded.

C1.reason: The agenda-setters' incentives are analysed only within equilibrium characterisations (EQ), with no separate result on manipulation or strategyproofness that would warrant SB.

value.quote: all citizens vote for one of the two proposals using majority
value.note: Input is a single vote for one proposal (plurality rule, reducing to majority between two proposals); not a profile of pairwise comparisons or a majority relation, so OTH (single-choice vote).

C2.2.reason: Each citizen casts a single plurality/majority vote for one proposal, which is not a pairwise-comparison profile or majority relation as PAIR denotes.

value.loc: Sect. 3.4, p. 111; Sect. 5.1, p. 120; Appendix A, p. 123
value.note: Voting decisions are a separate component of the equilibrium strategy profile, distinct from the utilities u_j; Appendix A derives voting behaviour from utility comparisons, and 'truthfully' presupposes that votes could differ from utilities.

C2.4.reason: Votes are modelled as equilibrium actions distinct from utilities u_j (separate objects, behaviour derived in Appendix A), so the paper treats input and held attitude as separate rather than equating them.

value.note: C2.2 = OTH only; none of RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR, so the applicability condition is not met.

C4.1.reason: With C2.2 coded OTH the applicability condition for C4.1 fails.

value.quote_behav: planner should choose if s/he aims to maximize the utilitarian welfare
value.quote_info: might also be unknown when the decision-making procedure needs to be chosen
value.note: The benevolent planner's objective (utilitarian welfare) is stated explicitly (Definition 1), and Sect. 5.2 formalises the choice of procedure behind a veil of ignorance (Proposition 6), with parameters known only via distributions.

C6.DES.reason: The paper explicitly states the planner's welfare objective and formally models the choice of procedure in Sect. 5.2 and Proposition 6, meeting the DES condition.

value.quote: as is standard, citizens vote as if they were pivotal
value.note: Only an appeal to standard practice in prior work, with no argument for treating voters and agenda-setters differently; consistent with C3.3 = CONV.

C7.2.reason: The only justification is the appeal 'as is standard' to prior practice, which is a convention/citation-type reference rather than an argument, matching CITE (consistent with C3.3 = CONV).
